```{r setup, include = F}
# Set Options ==================================================================
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = '-')

# Import =======================================================================
library(here)
library(openxlsx)
library(srvyr)
library(tidyverse)

casper_clean <- readRDS(here("data/casper_2026_clean.rds"))

# Convert to srvyr design
srv_design <- as_survey_design(casper_clean,
                               ids = surv_cluster,
                               weights = surv_weight)

# Worker Functions =============================================================
# Function for getting summaries of factors ------------------------------------
# NOTE: Can only accept 1 variable at a time
summarize_factor <- function(var_name) {
  
  # TODO: Consider keeping NA's, why are we removing?
  #  - How does it handle places where the data are skipped?
  #  - Want to show % of people where whole is number that saw the question
  a <- srv_design %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var_name]]))
  
  # Break if all data are NA
  if (nrow(a)==0){
    warning("No non-missing observations for ", var_name)
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Make sure this variable is a factor
  if (!is.factor(pull(a, var_name))) {
    a <- a %>%
      mutate(across(all_of(var_name), as.factor))
  }
  
  # Get factor levels for later joining
  level_df <- data.frame(
    Category = levels(pull(a, var_name))
  )
  level_df$Variable <- var_name
  
  a %>%
    # grouping by values in each variable
    group_by(.data[[var_name]]) %>%
    summarize(
      # count of responses for each variable
      Frequency = n(),
      Estimated_HH = round(survey_total(vartype = "var"), 0),
      # Calculates the weighted percentage of the population that falls into this category
      # The vartype = "ci" tells R to automatically calculate the 95% CIs
      Percent = round(
        survey_prop(vartype = c("ci", "se"), 
                    prop_method = "likelihood",
                    proportion = TRUE
                    ) * 100, 
        2)) %>%
    # lists var_names in a column called category
    mutate(Variable = var_name, Category = .data[[var_name]]) %>%
    # Bring in factor levels that may have been blank
    full_join(level_df, by = c("Variable", "Category")) %>%
    mutate(Category = factor(Category, levels = level_df$Category),
           pct_ci = if_else(
             is.na(Percent),
             "-",
             paste0(round(Percent_low, 2), " - ", round(Percent_upp, 2)))
           ) %>%
    arrange(Category) %>%
    # Only keep wanted cols
    select(Question = Variable,
           Answer = Category,
           N = Frequency,
           `Est HH`=Estimated_HH,
           Pct=Percent,
           `Pct 95CI` = pct_ci,
           `Pct SE` = Percent_se)
}

# Function for getting summaries of numerics -----------------------------------
summarize_numeric <- function(var_name) {
  num_results <- srv_design %>%
    summarize(
      median = survey_quantile(
        .data[[var_name]],
        quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
        na.rm = TRUE,
        vartype = "ci"
      ),
      mean = survey_mean(
        .data[[var_name]],
        vartype = "ci",
        na.rm = T
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      median_ci = paste0(median_q50_low, " - ", median_q50_upp),
      iqr = paste0(median_q25, " - ", median_q75),
      mean = round(mean, 2),
      mean_ci = paste0(round(mean_low, 2), " - ", round(mean_upp, 2))
    )
  
  tibble(
    Question = var_name,
    Median = num_results$median_q50,
    `Median 95CI` = num_results$median_ci,
    IQR = num_results$iqr,
    Mean = num_results$mean,
    `Mean 95CI` = num_results$mean_ci
  )
}
```

# Demographics

```{r tables}
# Means
demo_n <- c("demo_n_hh", "demo_n_u2", "demo_n_2to17", "demo_n_18to64", "demo_n_65p")
demo_n_table <- map(demo_n, summarize_numeric) %>%
  list_rbind()
knitr::kable(demo_n_table)

demo_factor <- c(
  "demo_hh_infants", "demo_hh_kids", "demo_hh_adults", "demo_hh_elders",
  "demo_own_rent", "demo_langs"
)
demo_table <- map(demo_factor, summarize_factor) %>%
  list_rbind()
knitr::kable(demo_table)
```

# Disaster Experience

```{r disaster_experience}
# Disaster experience variables
NDexp_vars <- c(
  "NDexp_affected", "NDexp_displaced", "NDexp_damage",
  "NDexp_type_hurricane", "NDexp_type_none", "NDexp_type_flood",
  "NDexp_type_tsunami", "NDexp_type_earthquake", "NDexp_type_eruption",
  "NDexp_type_landslide", "NDexp_type_wildfire", "NDexp_type_unsure",
  "NDexp_prepared", "NDexp_safe"
)

NDexp_table <- map(NDexp_vars, summarize_factor) %>%
  list_rbind()
knitr::kable(NDexp_table)

NDexp_n_table <- summarize_numeric("NDexp_displaced_days")
knitr::kable(NDexp_n_table)
```

```{r export}
# Put tables into Excel file ---------------------------------------------------
# Combine tables into a list so that each is its own sheet
my_sheets <- list(
  "Numerics"          = bind_rows(demo_n_table, NDexp_n_table),
  "Demographics"      = demo_table,
  "Natural Disasters" = NDexp_table,
  "Evacuation"        = evac_table,
  "Supplies"          = supp_table,
  "Health"            = health_table
)

write.xlsx(my_sheets, file = here("KonaCASPER2026_datatables.xlsx"))

# Export tables ----------------------------------------------------------------
saveRDS(srv_design, file = here("data/srv_design.rds"))
saveRDS(demo_table, file = here("data/demo_table.rds"))
saveRDS(NDexp_table, file = here("data/NDexp_table.rds"))
saveRDS(evac_table, file = here("data/evac_table.rds"))
saveRDS(supp_table, file = here("data/supp_table.rds"))
saveRDS(health_table, file = here("data/health_table.rds"))
```
